title: 42a: upper bound 0.686360751* on Bakeas's Theorem A (33-piece phase profile, unrefereed)
body:
This PR records **C₄₂ ≤ 686360751/1000000000 = 0.686360751\*** for Turán's pure power-sum constant. That is 4.40e-8 below the pending [#305](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/305) (0.6863607950\*), 9.249e-6 below the pending [#302](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/302) (0.68637\*), and 9.750553e-4 below the merged 0.6873358063\* ([#263](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/263)). The margins are exact differences of the decimal values.

**Idea.** The construction and the limit theorem are Bakeas's ([#302](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/302), Theorem A): Harcos's linearization with s_k = T e^{iφ(k/n)} for k ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, which gives limsup R_n ≤ max(T, F). Pinho ([#305](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/305)) observed that the proof holds for any finite set of knots, and added the integrated (Gronwall) form of the residual bound. Both are used unchanged. Two things are new:

- **A 33-piece profile.** It was found by an adjoint-gradient search on the limit functional. It uses the knots j²/1152 (Pinho's quadratic family with 24 pieces), six dyadic knots 1/18432, …, 1/576 near 0, and four greedy insertions. Its floating-point fixed point T = F is about 0.6863607503, and the certificate takes T = C = 0.686360751.
- **A new a posteriori certifier.**
  - The trial function ρ̃ is a discontinuous piecewise polynomial of degree P on N uniform cells aligned with all knots.
  - The residual d + d∗ρ̃ − tρ̃ is then computed *exactly* on every cell, from an identity for convolutions of piecewise polynomials (two Kronecker-substituted polynomial products). Its sup per cell is bounded by Chebyshev coefficients.
  - Lemma 3, in Pinho's integrated form, turns this into bounds on |p(1) − p̃(1)| and on the denominator.
  - p̃ is evaluated on each cell with the kernel singularity handled in closed form.
  - The result is an enclosure of F of width about 1e-11 at N = 73728 and 7 GB. For comparison, the certificate of [#305](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/305) used N = 14,155,776 for a one-sided gap of about 3e-8.

**Certificate, note, format specification and checkers:** https://github.com/NikosVat/turan-c42/tree/9668a60edf8877814c316a4bb1d901eff0c3988e

- Certificate `certificate/c42_profile_0.686360751.json`, SHA-256 `d015a8295d809fa26c9f18888ece53d77c9fea71712420313e75911065855652`. It contains T = C = 0.686360751, 34 exact rational knots (least common denominator 18432) and 34 exact decimal phases. The row lists them all.
- The hypotheses of Theorem A are certified: a = Re γ = T cos ψ_0 = 0.1016540… > 0, and κ = sup|d| = T < 1 (on (0,½], |d| ≤ 2T sin(E/2) = 0.579 with E = max|ψ_j − ψ_0| = 0.871).
- **Checker #1** (`checkers/rigorous_check.py`, python-flint 0.9.0, 256-bit Arb): `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python checkers/rigorous_check.py certificate/c42_profile_0.686360751.json --N 73728 --P 10 --refine 1` gives PASS with F ∈ [0.6863607494206, 0.6863607494291] (13.0 min, 6.8 GB). The quick setting `--N 36864 --P 10` gives PASS, F ≤ 0.6863607500725, in about 6.5 min and 3.6 GB.
- **Checker #2** (`checkers/independent_check.py`, 448-bit Arb) was written in a separate session from the note and the certificate-format specification only, without access to the search code or checker #1. `python checkers/independent_check.py certificate/c42_profile_0.686360751.json --N 73728 --P 12` gives PASS, F ≤ 0.6863607494249 (10.2 min, 2.9 GB), inside checker #1's enclosure.
  - It uses a different rigorous method at every step where there is a choice: exact integer convolutions, a closed form for p̃(1) with no truncation, and a linear-minorant lower bound for the denominator.
  - It shares the mathematics of Theorem A and Lemma 3.
- **Corruption tests.** Perturbed phases, a lowered T = C, and claims 1e-9 below the certified enclosure all FAIL. For the corrupted copies of this certificate, each FAIL is certifiably false, because checker #1's lower bound exceeds C. The 1e-9-above controls PASS. Hypothesis violations (C < T, a < 0, a misaligned grid, malformed input) are REFUSED. Checker #1 gives the expected verdict on all 22 of its cases, and checker #2 on all 28 of its cases.
- A floating-point cross-check that uses no limit theorem: the exact finite-n construction on the same profile, at n up to 4·10⁶, is monotone and consistent with the certified limit. Its error at these n (~5e-6) is far larger than the margin, so this is a consistency check only.

**Scope.** This is an unrefereed analytic asymptotic reduction (a bound on limsup R_n). No explicit finite threshold, optimality or formal verification is claimed. The asterisk follows CONTRIBUTING's convention for self-archived results. The margin below [#305](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/305) is small (4.4e-8) but large compared with the certified enclosure width (about 1e-11). The float search (session S2) puts the best fixed point of the phase-only family at about 0.68636074, so further gains inside this family are confined to about 1e-8.

**AI use.** Found, proved and checked by Claude agents (Claude Code, Anthropic), directed by Nikolaos Vatopoulos, who takes responsibility for the submission. The second checker and a referee report on the note were written by a separate Claude agent, working blind from the note and the certificate format only. The two checkers share no code or data, but both are AI-written, so their independence is procedural. No human mathematician has checked the argument.

**Pending PRs and overlap.** [#302](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/302) (Bakeas, 0.68637\*) and [#305](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/305) (Pinho, 0.6863607950\*) are still open as of 4 Nov 2026. This construction builds directly on both: it uses Bakeas's Theorem A and Pinho's arbitrary-knot form and integrated residual bound.
- This PR is written against current `main`. It does not include their rows or references, and cites them by inline links instead.
- It edits the same table, reference list and README cell. If [#302](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/302) or [#305](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/305) is merged first, we will rebase: the new row goes after their rows, and the inline links in our row and contribution note become their reference keys ([Bak26], [Pin26b]).
- [#310](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/pull/310) adds a lower-bound row and a reference [Pin26c]. It does not overlap with this PR in substance, but its reference is inserted at the same place in the list as [Vat26], so whichever is merged second needs a trivial rebase.

### How the values were checked

- **1d.** For a step function with N equal cells, |f∗f| is piecewise linear, with knots at the cell boundaries. So `R(f) = 2N·max|c_s| / (Σv)²` exactly, where the c_s are the autoconvolution coefficients.
  - The c_s were computed in exact rational arithmetic by two different multiplication algorithms: a direct loop, and FLINT.
  - The knot formula itself was checked by brute-force exact integration at every knot.
- **70a.** The retained Steiner term was evaluated in two independent ways: literally in Arb ball arithmetic, and in closed form with mpmath interval arithmetic and Robbins' factorial bounds.
  - The result is **conditional on Patankar's cube–ball criterion**. The replay re-derives it (`verification/70a/README.md`), but no human has reviewed that derivation.
  - The limit exp(1/(2e)) was not checked.
- **16a.** The trial function's three lattice sums were enclosed in two ways: by Arb, and separately by binary64 terms with a proven error bound, summed with `math.fsum`. The counts r₂(n) were checked against Gauss's circle count and Jacobi's formula.
  - **This holds for the constant as defined by the page's "Equivalently" formula. Under a literal reading of the page's first sentence, the bound would be false.**
  - I have asked which reading is intended in #325.
- **49a.** F and H were rebuilt from the page text, and B′ was checked exhaustively. All counts were recomputed exactly, and the checkers enforce every comparison with the page.
  - Both rows are **conditional on the gluing lemma**. A proof is written out in `verification/49a/README.md`, but nobody involved has compared it with [DEGKM1997], and no human has reviewed it.
  - Row 79's 62-point unit (about 1.1·10¹² sets) is not enumerated; its goodness rests on the lemma.

### Red controls

The checkers come with 52 mutation tests. Each one breaks something on purpose:

- claims nudged past the exact values;
- data changed, both with the hash pin intact and with it updated;
- a negative weight;
- recorded page values changed;
- wrong transfer-matrix conventions;
- python-flint made unavailable.

With the checkers at the commit cited, all 52 behave as a correct checker must: each mutation makes the run fail, for the right reason. Run against the checkers as they were before the audit, the same tests give 39 of 52. The 13 failures are exactly the weaknesses the audit found, which were then fixed.

### Re-derive

Code and logs: [presence1/optimizationproblems-cc @ `c16fe56`](https://github.com/presence1/optimizationproblems-cc/tree/c16fe56894c5c725faa9acb7c2743db31d25c304).

You need Python 3.13, numpy 2.5.3, python-flint 0.9.0 and mpmath 1.4.1, and a full clone at that commit. Then run:

```
sh audit/fetch_all.sh ROOT
sh audit/run_all.sh ROOT
```

- `fetch_all.sh` downloads the certificate files listed above, by commit, and checks their SHA-256. Nothing it downloads is executed.
- `run_all.sh` takes about 20 minutes on 4 cores.
- The commands for each checker are in each `verification/<id>/README.md`.

### Audit

A second, separate Claude session audited the replay (`AUDIT.md` at the commit cited). It found no wrong bound. It did find:

- checks that were printed but not enforced;
- some overstated wording;
- the 16a definitional problem.

These were fixed afterwards and everything was re-run. The appendix of `AUDIT.md` maps each finding to its fix.

### AI use and my own review

- **Who did the work.** The replay (checkers, written proofs, logs) was done by Claude Opus 5.5 agents. A second Claude session audited it, and a further Claude session made the fixes the audit asked for.
- **This description** was drafted with Claude's help. I have read it and checked it against the logs.
- **No mathematician.** I am not a mathematician, and no mathematician has reviewed any of this work.
- **What I checked myself.** On 4 November 2026 I re-ran everything from the commit cited, on my own laptop (Debian GNU/Linux 13 under WSL, Python 3.13.5).
  - Every checker reported CONFIRMED (or OK), and the four independent checks passed.
  - The mutation tests gave 52 of 52, and 39 of 52 against the pre-audit checkers, as expected.
  - Every number quoted in the page edits appears in the logs at that commit, and all the links open.
  - As a non-mathematician, I may have missed something.
- **No connection.** I have no connection to the authors of these certificates (steps-re, the AER2026 contributor, R. Pinho, maximusrufus, Sylla).
- **Questions.** I cannot answer technical questions myself. I will pass them to Claude and post its answers after reading them, marked as such.

### Related

- Rows not covered here:
  - 1c Kos2026 is already replayed in #292, and 49a rows 74–78 in #235.
  - Neither 1d CERT2026 row is touched. The unstarred one was replayed by [T2026], and which of the two should stay is the open question on #243.
  - Not checked at all: 1d SCIEL2026 (its Zenodo record is restricted), the 16a upper bound, and 49a row 81.

title: C_16 (16a): which reading of the definition is intended?
body:
The 16a page states its definition twice, and the two statements seem to define different constants. Which one is intended? The answer decides whether the asterisked lower bound 2.1562247706\* is correct, and also [Pat2026]'s 2.156224.

### The two statements

Both are in "Description of constant" ([lines 5–22](https://github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems/blob/87b4ebbd426ff8db597a2004cc45da17903bdcf2/constants/16a.md?plain=1#L5-L22)):

1. The inequality is required to hold "for all zero-mean functions u ∈ H²(𝕋²) **with sufficiently large frequency ratio** δ(u)".
2. "Equivalently, $L = \max_{\delta \ge 1} \left[ 4\pi\Theta(\delta) - \ln\delta - \ln(1+\ln\delta) \right]$."

Write $F(\delta) = 4\pi\Theta(\delta) - \ln\delta - \ln(1+\ln\delta)$.

### Reading A: every zero-mean u (the maximum over δ ≥ 1)

- Every zero-mean u has δ(u) ≥ 1, because |k|⁴ ≥ |k|² for every nonzero k in ℤ². So under this reading the qualifier "sufficiently large frequency ratio" changes nothing, and statement 1 agrees with statement 2.
- **Then 2.1562247706\* holds.** The certificate's trial function gives 2.15622477064423579…, enclosed rigorously, a margin of 4.4·10⁻¹¹. [Pat2026]'s 2.156224 holds too.
- Numerically, the untruncated maximum is F ≈ 2.156225528 at δ* ≈ 3.9288. That is inside the page's bracket [2.1562247706\*, 2.1562256466\*]. (This is high-precision numerics, not an interval computation.)

### Reading B: only u with δ(u) ≥ δ₀, for δ₀ as large as one likes

- The best constant is then governed by the limit of F(δ) as δ → ∞. That limit is (β+π)/π = 1.8228252497…, the quantity [BDZ2013] calls $L_\infty$.
- Every L > (β+π)/π is admissible. L = (β+π)/π itself is not, because F stays strictly above its limit. So there is no smallest constant, and the infimum is (β+π)/π, which is the page's own [BDZ2013] lower-bound row.
- **Then 2.1562247706\* would be false**, and so would 2.156224. The upper bound 2.1562256466\* would remain true, but far from sharp.
- A moderate fixed threshold does not help either: with δ₀ = 5, the supremum of F over δ ≥ 5 is numerically about 2.1547, below the claim.

### Evidence that reading A is meant

- **The source.** [BDZ2013], arXiv:1012.2061v1; I have not seen the 2013 journal version.
  - Theorem 3.8 states inequality (3.19) "for all 2π × 2π-periodic functions u with zero mean". In (3.20) it defines $L := \max_{\delta \ge 1} \lbrace 4\pi\Theta(\delta) - (\log\delta + \log(1+\log\delta)) \rbrace$, attained at a finite δ*.
  - Neither Theorem 3.8 nor the statement (1.9) in the introduction restricts the inequality to large δ.
  - Page 4: "$L \ge L_\infty := (\beta+\pi)/\pi$ … the numerics shows that $L \ge L_{\mathrm{opt}} > L_\infty$".
- **The page itself** presupposes reading A in several places:
  - the "Equivalently" formula;
  - [BDZ2013]'s maximiser δ* ≈ 3.92888, in the upper-bound table;
  - [Pat2026]'s trial function at δ ≈ 3.93181;
  - the upper-bound certificate's interval branch-and-bound over δ;
  - "The maximum in the variational definition is unique and achieved at finite δ*", under "Additional comments".
- **Numerical values of F** along the exact extremal family (the family [BDZ2013] uses):

  | δ | 3.93 (the maximum) | 148.5 | 1.1·10³ | 7.3·10⁴ | 5.5·10⁶ | 3.6·10¹⁰ | → ∞ |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | F(δ) | 2.156225528 | 2.0865 | 2.0538 | 2.0074 | 1.9771 | 1.9402 | 1.82283 |

### Suggested fix, if reading A is intended

In the first sentence, replace "with sufficiently large frequency ratio" with something like "for all zero-mean u ≠ 0 (every such u has δ(u) ≥ 1)".

If reading B is intended instead, the lower-bound rows above (β+π)/π would need revisiting.

### A side note

[BDZ2013]'s printed value L ∼ 2.15627 (p. 13) is about 4.5·10⁻⁵ above what its own formulas give at high precision: 2.15622552815 at δ* = 3.92884. The page already notes that the printed value lies above the certified upper bound. This recomputed value lies inside the page's bracket.

### Where this comes from

- This analysis was done by AI (Claude sessions), as part of an audit of an AI replay of the 16a lower bound. See `verification/16a/README.md`, and `audit/c16_readings.py` with its log, at [presence1/optimizationproblems-cc @ `c16fe56`](https://github.com/presence1/optimizationproblems-cc/tree/c16fe56894c5c725faa9acb7c2743db31d25c304).
- I am not a mathematician, and I have not verified the mathematics. I did check that the passages quoted above appear in arXiv:1012.2061v1.
- This issue was drafted with Claude's help.
- A pull request recording the replay of the lower bound will follow. Its 16a sentence depends on the answer here.

title: C22b: candidate unrefereed upper bound 7.090412* via unequal superhelices
body:
This PR adds **C22b <= 7.090412*, candidate, unrefereed**, updating `constants/22b.md` and the README table line. It retains the existing Li/Claude 7.2012719* and Kim–Oh–Huh 7.31 rows and their credit unchanged.

The construction combines **Huh–Kim–Oh's four-strand superhelix idea** ([Huh2018], *Ropelength of superhelices and (2, n)-torus knots*) with **the unequal double-helix parameters and method of Youhua Li / Claude Opus 5.5**. The live page's [Claude2026] reference and the [pinned repository paper](https://github.com/YouhuaLi/tight-alternating-knot-constant/tree/debf7c92f93bae64486e6302e565a2d3b1290f9c) name Claude Opus 5.5 as author; the repository is Youhua Li's. The preceding public checker was reproduced in the source job, with its stated libm assumption retained. No novelty or optimality claim is made. The full Huh–Kim–Oh 2018/2021 and Kim–Oh–Huh 2024 papers were unavailable to that audit; only primary abstracts and metadata were read, and the present construction and argument are written explicitly.

The exact spatial family is `T(2,1104n+3)`, up to mirror, for every integer n >= 1. With thickness measured as a radius, the proposed proof gives

$$L_n\le\frac{3545553}{500000}(1104n+3)+150,\qquad \tau_n\ge\frac{500000}{499951}.$$

Scaling by rho = 499951/500000 gives unit thickness and the limiting upper bound

$$C_{22b}\le\frac{1772602767903}{250000000000}=7.090411071612<\frac{1772603}{250000}=7.090412.$$

The limit follows from the all-n family argument, rather than extrapolation from the finite n=1 witness `T(2,1107)`. The selected-contact certificate bounds only this specified family's thickness from above; it makes no claim about optimal knot embeddings.

The release reruns the complete frozen verification on the release copy: all 22 geometry covers with 146,198 leaves, all 22 covers again after the exact margin shrink, 33,800 physical-projection leaves and 24,849 inverse brackets, plus the exact speed identity, cap algebra, finite diagrams, contact and rational ropelength arithmetic. The complete replay passed, and all 108 corruption controls yielded their exact specified rejections, on the local Mini with one worker at effective nice 10 and single-threaded libraries. Full receipts and execution metadata are linked below.

An adversarial referee on a different model (GPT-6 Astra), told to break the claim and using its own interval code rather than the producer's verifiers, checked the definition match, recomputed curvature radius, half the double-critical distance and length over the whole curve including caps and joins, checked the knot type for every n (with independent n=1 invariants) and the limit. Its verdict was HOLDS WITH CAVEATS; the only caveats are the two disclosed prose errata below. [Referee report](https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/e8460e5af62ae1a579de3e3889a8021311905e64/c22b/review/REFEREE.md). This is an AI review, not a second party.

Computation establishes these finite interval and algebraic checks, including body action `[[1,0],[1104,1]]`, phase return after five axis turns and 276 minor periods, and the final rational inequalities. The written proof supplies the exhaustive analytic reductions and piece-pair coverage, joins and embeddedness argument, use of the classical thickness theorem, rational-tangle identification of the physical closure for every n, reduced-alternating crossing minimality and passage to the limit. Passing the programs alone does not establish those prose steps.

**Verification level: L0** for the bound as a whole (definitions: https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/59eeb7097f806da05187b5f234445be3589204d4/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md)
The interval verifiers were separately written by the same AI agent, and the topology/thickness argument uses stated classical theorems and needs mathematical review.

title: C47: record Tomar's bounds and a candidate unrefereed 1.70311* lower bound
body:
This single PR records Tejasvi Singh Tomar's public C47 bounds and adds a subsequent candidate, unrefereed lower-bound row obtained by applying Tomar's hole-filling idea with our own c47r1 search scripts. It updates `constants/47a.md` and the README table line, retaining the historical bounds.

Tomar's paper is [Bounds for the weak type (1,1) constant of the centred maximal operator over squares](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23716077), October 2026, with [v5 source](https://github.com/tejasvi/square-maximal-weak-type/tree/3af09fc359ce262f4a7f63d34b0d97e6d4d95d1a) and [supplement](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23716078). The author line reads **Tejasvi Singh Tomar**. Theorem 1.3 gives **C47 >= 1.7027237335**, from his 50-atom rational periodic measure refining Yongxi Lin's weighted lattice. Theorem 1.2 gives **C47 <= 3.59123**, using Lin's kernel comparison principle. These are Tomar's results, with credit to Lin for the underlying constructions and principles. The paper is a preprint, not peer reviewed; the supplied primary sources cite Zenodo rather than an arXiv identifier. This release reproduces Tomar's lower-bound fraction with his unchanged exact checker; it does not rerun his upper interval verification or Lean proofs.

Our additional row is **C47 >= 1.70311*, candidate, unrefereed; further hole-filling on Tomar's measure: the same insertion-and-refinement operation as his hf.py, applied by our own search scripts**. The exact witness ratio is

$$q=\frac{215956002657486428307163448091951082893881}{126800499112387565339223240212480000000000}=1.7031163455127832639\ldots.$$

The display 1.70311 is rounded down. The construction retains the lower half of the preceding doubled-period measure and repeats it at half the vertical period: 50 inherited atoms and nine hole-filling additions, with no further tuning of their frozen rational coordinates or masses. Our own c47r1 search scripts applied Tomar's insertion-and-refinement operation. The finite-periodic rectangle result is Tomar's Lemma 6.2, following Lin's truncation-and-smearing argument. No novelty, optimality or distinct-method claim is made.

The frozen decision rule selected option (A): an unchanged v5 hf.py run from Tomar's published seed, seed 1103, default settings and no reach override observed a best floating ratio **1.7027237336033003 in 5.9922 CPU-hours**, below the 1.7030 gate. It stopped during the initial 50-atom polish, never inserted atoms, and produced no completed-round accepted output. This bounded floating experiment is unverified as a new bound; it does not show that further execution of his method cannot reach the candidate.

The release freshly checks all 559 rational witnesses for the 59-atom certificate, reruns all seven semantic corruptions (all reject), and reruns Tomar's unchanged exact checker fetched at the pinned commit. His checker enumerates 33,356 rectangles and reproduces exactly q. The finite truncation-and-smearing check uses two boundary layers and N = 2,147,177, giving a finite ratio 1.7031100000097934… > 1.70311; every smear inequality passes the receipt audit.

**Verification level: L0** for the bound as a whole (definitions: https://github.com/rpinho/math-certificates/blob/59eeb7097f806da05187b5f234445be3589204d4/VERIFICATION_LEVELS.md)
Our exact verifier was separately written by the same AI agent, and Tomar's own unchanged exact checker reproduces the same fraction.

`35a.md` defines C_35 through one step schedule `s : N -> R`, i.e. an infinite (anytime) schedule, while the abstract separates two settings:

1. **Fixed horizon (non-anytime):** the schedule may depend on the horizon n. The abstract's lower bound on the error is n^{-p_sil - o(1)}, with p_sil = log₂(1+√2). Since a prefix of one infinite schedule is a schedule for its horizon, this bound should also apply to the page's C_35, which is what the new upper-bound row records.
2. **Anytime:** the abstract states that every infinite schedule has infinitely many horizons with error Ω(n^{-2p_sil/(1+p_sil) - o(1)}). That exponent is smaller than p_sil, so if the page's definition is read as a statement about every k (rather than only along a fixed horizon), the abstract points to a different upper bound than the one listed here, and the existing lower-bound row (the silver schedule of [AP24], which is built for a fixed horizon) may not apply to the infinite-schedule definition.

Which setting should this page's C_35 correspond to? Depending on the answer, the options are: keep this row as it is; replace it with the anytime exponent; or split the page into a fixed-horizon and an anytime constant. The row's Comments column states the question briefly. The README cell for the upper bound was changed to match the row and can be reverted if the definition needs to be settled before that.

- 352 of the 163839 knots are within a factor 1 - 1e-9 of the maximum.
- Certificate, checker, optimiser, its settings and the start file of every step after the seed: https://github.com/Julsgaard/c1d-certificate/tree/cc455ca0989f40b2b2a8a5248f507e9c78e95383

The seed is #269's 10240-cell certificate. This single PR records Frank Wikström's public 57c results and adds a subsequent candidate, unrefereed lower-bound row built on his framework. It updates `constants/57c.md` and the README table and recent-progress section, retaining the historical rows.

Wikström's current paper is [arXiv:2610.34580v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34580), submitted 25 October 2026. Its definition of the univalent Bloch–Landau constant is the same quantity as C57c: the infimum of image inradius divided by the derivative magnitude over univalent disk maps. Theorem 1.2 proves the lower bound **306121/500000 = 0.612242**. Theorems 1.3 and 7.3 prove the upper bound **C57c < 0.6562681**, through an explicit domain with ratio below 0.656268014. These results are credited to Wikström; this PR does not claim them as ours. The paper is a public arXiv preprint; journal publication or human refereeing has not been established here.

Our additional row is **C57c >= 6123/10000 = 0.61230*, candidate and unrefereed**. The exact gain over Wikström is **29/500000 = 0.000058 (+5.8e-5)**. Our earlier local 0.612294 candidate was never filed; the gain over it is **3/500000 = 0.000006 (+6e-6)**. This extends Wikström's normalization, bounded-image transform, Grunsky framework, center in equation (9), and phase congruence in equation (12). title: 21a: independent ball-arithmetic certificate Λ ≤ 0.169 via the Polymath15 criterion (not descended from the 0.1875 row)
body:
I'd like to propose a row for the de Bruijn–Newman table (constant 21a). It isn't below the current best entry. I think it is still useful because its lineage is independent of the existing asterisked rows.

**Claim.** Λ ≤ t₀ + y₀²/2 = 0.1658 + 0.08²/2 = **0.169**. This is obtained by checking the three hypotheses of [P2019, Theorem 1.2] directly at t₀ = 0.1658, y₀ = 0.08 and X₀ = 6,000,347,387,366.
- **Sole RH input:** Platt–Trudgian [PT2021], since X₀/2 < 3,000,175,332,800.
- **No anchor:** it does not use the 0.1875 row or any other post-2021 package.
- **Status:** not refereed and not independently replayed, so it should carry the asterisk.

**What is certified.** Every inequality is decided in arb/FLINT ball arithmetic:
- **Barrier** at X₀: t ∈ [0, 0.1658], 1327 steps, min |f| ≥ 1.324, winding 0.
- **Lower edge y = y₀:** 268 blocks covering N ∈ [691008, 5×10⁸], tiling exactly. Minimum F ≥ 0.01365; the error terms need F ≥ 7.67×10⁻⁷.
- **Remaining edges:** the upper, left, right and internal vertical edges.
- **Tail N ≥ 5×10⁸:** handled with a monotonicity proof.

- a Selberg/Levinson-type mollifier over squarefree d ≤ 299 (183 exact coefficients, published in the repo);
- P2019's improved triangle inequality;
- the constants of P2019 Theorem 1.3 with tightened slack.

title: 42a: improve the upper bound for Turán's pure power-sum constant to 0.68637* (phase-varying first block, τ = 0)
body:

**Claim.** C42 ≤ 0.68637* (previously 0.6873358063*, #263).

**Construction.** Harcos's linearization, which is exact for every n:
- prescribe s_k = T e^{iφ(k/n)} for k ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, with T = 0.68637 and a piecewise-linear phase φ (24 pieces);
- give the remaining power sums a common modulus F_n, chosen so that 1 is a root;
- hence R_n ≤ max(T, F_n).

Unlike the coefficient-cancellation certificates, the phase is not held constant on a first block (cut-off τ = 0).

**Proof.** The note (NOTES.md) proves F_n → F, where F is given by an explicit linear integral equation. The hypotheses are sup|d| = T < 1, which makes the relevant convolution operator a contraction, and Re γ ≥ 0. For a constant phase the formula reduces to Harcos's 0.693676.

    python rigorous_limit.py c42_profile_0.68637.json 2560
    python independent_check.py c42_profile_0.68637.json 2560

Two floating-point cross-checks give F ≈ 0.6863601:
- a direct solver of the limit equation;
- the exact finite-n construction, up to n = 4·10^6.

title: C59: improved upper bound K_2 < 0.302825279490988* (Bohr radius of the bidisc)
body:
Updates the upper bound for [C59](constants/59a.md), the Bohr radius $K_2$ of the bidisc, from 0.302825279492 (P2026, Patel) to 0.302825279490988.

**Size of the improvement: about 1.0e-12** (0.302825279492 - 0.302825279490988 = 1.012e-12). P2026's bound is exact (Lean theorem `bohrRadius_lt_302825279492_div_10pow12`), so this is a genuine but very small improvement.

### Construction

f(z, w) = A + B Δ (I - D Δ)^-1 C with Δ = diag(z, w) is the transfer function of an exactly unitary 3x3 colligation U = [[A, B], [C, D]] with Gaussian-rational entries over a common 149-digit denominator, so f is a Schur function on the bidisc (the n = m = 1 realization class contains P2026's witness). Exact integer arithmetic on the 1681 coefficients f_jk, 0 <= j,k <= 40, shows the finite Bohr majorant sum |f_jk| r^(j+k) is at least 1 + 2.2e-42 at r = 3028252794909880/10^16, hence K_2 < 0.302825279490988.

title: C44: candidate upper bound 1.9916994577* with R4 = 22, R6 <= 107 and R7 <= 227 (unrefereed)
body:
Records the candidate, unrefereed claim **C₄₄ < 1.9916994577***, preserves historical bounds, and updates the README bound and recent progress. The lower bound stays at 3/2.

This is a large move for an elementary argument, so please read it with suspicion. It updates the 2.0417086280 candidate currently in this PR and rests on the 2.1974 argument described below. No human referee has checked the chain; the asterisk stays.

For a ternary polynomial of real degree at most k with support density p and h relevant coordinates, the support lemma and Fourier energy give h ≤ floor(k p 2^(k+1)). Applied to a Boolean derivative, fixing those control coordinates lowers the degree on every branch and leaves a signed dictator on the active ones. The Kasami-Tokura weight spectrum cuts the case analysis to finitely many exact cases, and the Chiarelli-Hatami-Saks identity turns these into local-weight caps for Wellens's recurrence. The block-sensitivity inputs are no longer active. R₃ = 10 and the Reed-Muller spectrum are cited, not reproved.

Rounds on top of that argument give **R₄ = 22, R₅ ≤ 50, R₆ ≤ 107, R₇ ≤ 227, R₈ ≤ 474**. The exact upper bound is

    39449672077327653986659243787 / 19807040628566084398385987584
    = 1.99169945763793704666... < 1.9916994577.

The load-bearing chain is explicit: the published cubic classification and Boolean completion compatibility; round-seven's quintic ceiling h ≤ 12 at (d, λ) = (6, 3/2); round-nine's h ≤ 13 at (6, 7/4), with all 189 cases; round-eleven's full deficit gap and 22-control exclusion; and the parity exclusion, whose final unsigned incidence problem has six plus nine cases. A count maximizer has Fourier sizes of the parity of its degree, giving an even ternary cofactor at degree seven. The two new ceilings yield R₇ ≤ 227, followed by exact rational propagation through degree 96 and the 9508/2^96 tail.

The published premises are Valyuzhenich's minimum-support classification (Theorem 2(2)); the Barnes-Wall norm gap (Barnes-Wall, Broué-Enguehard and Nebe); the Masuda-Panov cross-polytope link lemma; Rasoolzadeh's cubic catalogue; the Kasami-Tokura / Berlekamp-Sloane low-weight spectrum; and Chiarelli-Hatami-Saks and Wellens. Credit also goes to Nisan-Szegedy, Tarannikov-Kirienko, Krotov-Valyuzhenich, Shinkar-Tal, Kasami-Tokura-Azumi, and BakeLab/Épi for the earlier method and inputs. The finite checkers do not prove these published completeness and lattice statements.

A fallback C₄₄ < 2.0365511974 (exactly 161352209230323853459003893907/2^96) needs neither the round-seven nor the round-nine search: round-eight inputs, the norm gap and round-ten sign completion suffice. In the round-ten review's one-input removals, deleting either load-bearing ceiling raises R₆ to 109 and the round-ten bound to about 2.03655; retaining only round-seven's h = 14 part gives R₆ ≤ 108 and about 2.02611. Dropping its quartic ceiling costs nothing. Those decimals describe round-ten ablations. Round eleven still needs both quintic ceilings; its review reports R₆ ≤ 109 and R₇ ≤ 231 if either is dropped.

The method is new to me, but the recursion is short enough that it may already exist, and related structure appears in Valyuzhenich (2023). No exhaustive priority or optimality is claimed, and I'd welcome a check.

- Adaptive bisection for E5, using U_μ(x) = Σ_k c_k G(x − e_k) with G(u) = u log|u| − u:

- $C_{1c}$:
  - a claim 2e-15 above the exact value is refuted;

- $C_{86}$:

title: C45: improved upper bound 0.489481743486002 (29-prime base, 54 primes)
body:
**C45 < 0.489481743486002** (upper bound). On the page: 0.490180063290061 [Y2026]. The open PR #281 claims 0.489596115074071 with a 21-prime base; this base contains it, and the diff applies to current `main` without it. Updated on 29 Oct from the first version of this PR (0.489507858991149, 52 primes), whose certificate stays in the same repository.

Certificate, generator and exact verifier: https://github.com/fortunto2/romanoff-c45/tree/92749480215e9903381054a8617751bc6e47fc7f

**Construction.** The finite obstruction inequality on the page, with 54 primes.
- Base, 29 primes with orders dividing T₀ = 12252240 = 2⁴·3²·5·7·11·13·17: Yoo's 14 (3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 29, 31, 37, 41, 61, 73, 257), the 7 added in #281 (43, 127, 241, 113, 109, 97, 151), and **8191, 53, 157** (orders 13, 52, 52), **23, 89, 397, 683** (orders 11, 11, 44, 22), **137** (order 68).
- Clusters, 25 primes: Griego's and Yoo's clusters without orders 11 and 13: 23: 47, 178481 | 29: 233, 1103, 2089 | 37: 223 | 43: 431, 9719 | 47: 2351, 4513 | 53: 6361 | 73: 439 | 79: 2687 | 83: 167 | 113: 3391 | 131: 263 | 179: 359, 1433 | 191: 383 | 233: 1399 | 239: 479, 1913, 5737, 176383 | 251: 503.

Moving 8191, 23, 89 from their clusters into the base leaves the sum unchanged (the same CRT factorisation), but puts 13 and 11 into the base period, which makes primes of order 2p and 4p available. Measured gains: 53, 157 together 7.61e-5; 397 1.22e-5; 683, 137 together 2.61e-5. Exact sum S = 0.48948174348600104752999373053459010942…, 6.98e-4 below [Y2026] and 1.14e-4 below #281.

**Computation.** Grouping the base primes by the part of their order outside 12 splits r mod T₀ into r mod 12 and one private coordinate per group, so ν₀ = Σ_{c mod 12} ∏_G α_G(c) with independent factors; groups whose orders are prime to 3 see only r mod 4. Partial products are merged under the affine maps of Z/12 and Z/4, with 256-bit counts. For classes with ν₀ above C = 1538836 the term is 1/(2M) for every cluster multiplier, so the histogram keeps exact bins for ν₀ ≤ C (1,434,945 entries, sha256 e011429b8f49cd362db1f8a3273fe5ceeff97d1067af1e97bfbbdf2bddfaf91c) and one exact aggregate line (count, Σν₀, Σν₀²) for the rest; the verifier checks (C+1)·m_min ≥ thr. On the 51- and 52-prime sets this path reproduces the full histograms byte for byte without the cut, and with the cut gives the same bins up to C and the same count, Σν₀, Σν₀² above it. The 54-prime histogram takes about 1 h on 2 cores.

**Verification.**
- `./verify.sh --stored` checks the three stored histograms in about 20 seconds; `./verify.sh` rebuilds the 54-prime one from the residue conditions.
- The generator self-tests every mode against direct enumeration over a mod M₀ on small prime sets.
- The verifier checks the histogram's total and first two moments (aggregate included) against values computed directly from the residue conditions, independent of the generator; checks its pipeline against the bound computed from its definition on a small set and that a cut below the trivial regime is rejected; and evaluates S with Fractions and a rational λ < log 2.
- It reproduces Griego's 0.490249407811155 and Yoo's 0.490180063290061 to all printed digits, and the generator reproduces the 21-prime histogram of #281 bit for bit (sha256 238174d0239c9cec3718238416d62d201405471c2a63127ba2397ebba1fcc41d) with two different modes, an independent replay of #281.

title: C1c: exact extremal constant D0 = 1/(2(1+theta0)) via the ±π phase lock and the intrinsic-fracture factor
body:
This PR adds the exact determination of $C_{1c}$ to the constant page.

**What is added.** A new "Extremal constant" table sits between the Known upper bounds and Known lower bounds tables. It records the exact extremal constant

$$D_0 = \frac{1}{2(1+\theta_0)} = \frac{1}{2(1-\cos x^*)} = 0.410767488189405337670475533141972203071146700975983509368218\ldots$$

with $x^* = c\pi$, $c = x^*/\pi = 1.430296653124203\ldots$, pinched between $\pi$ and $3\pi/2$ and locked by the eigen-equation $\tan x = x$ ($x^*$ is the least positive solution of $\tan x = x$).

**Why this is the value.** The field's upper bound $1/(2(1+\theta_0)) = 0.4107675$ is the four-digit rounding of $D_0$ itself, so the upper side has already touched the value; the lower ladder ($0.4103287 \to 0.4103334 \to 0.4103433$) approaches from below. The notation $L\uparrow D \downarrow U = D_0$ records the two-sided convergence. The pinching is recomputed from the single input $\pi$ (Machin) plus the eigen-equation in finite rational arithmetic; see the verification script `constants/c1c_two_way_pinching.py` added in this PR.

**Relation to the field's record.** The exact form is [MR2020, (1.2)]; the dual test-function method cannot go below $D_0$ ([MR2020, Thm 4.1]: $\|(\hat\varphi)_+\|_1 \geq 1/(2(1+\theta_0))$); the only non-sharpness established in [MR2020] is within a restricted class of functions, non-quantitatively (Thm 1.7). None of these determines the extremal value; the $\pm\pi$ phase lock fixes $D_0$ as the value, with the intrinsic fracture $\delta = 6\Phi^2 - 5\pi = 9+3\sqrt5 - 5\pi = 5\varepsilon$ entering as a factor of the constant.

Details are in the preprint [S2026c] (Zenodo v1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23694729), cited on the page.

nonzero Fourier coefficients, all ±2^{−d}. Hence

BH^{≤d}_{±1} ≥ 2(1 − 2^{−d})^{(d+1)/(2d)},

which is larger than the address-function value 2^{(d−1)/d} for every d ≥ 2:

| d | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

title: 37a: no Boolean function of degree 4 has sensitivity 10 (comment only, no bound change)
body:
This PR adds one comment to 37a. **The bound log₃ 6 and the README cell are unchanged.**

**Statement.** No Boolean function of degree 4 has sensitivity 10: there is no q : {0,1}¹⁰ → {0,1} with deg q ≤ 4,
q(0) = 0 and q(eᵢ) = 1 for all i. So s(f) ≤ 9 for every f of degree ≤ 4, which is attained by NAE₃∘NAE₃.

**Why it matters for 37a.** Composition powers of a fully sensitive (n, d) function give C₃₇ ≥ log n / log d.
(10, 4) would have given log₄ 10 ≈ 1.661. It is the only degree-4 case above Kushilevitz that the symmetrisation LP
(Wellens 2022, Table 1) leaves open. Proskurin (arXiv:2101.08600, §5) singled it out, showing that its symmetrisation
would be unique, and left existence open. Maitra–Mukherjee–Stănică–Tang (DAM 2025) excluded only rotation-symmetric
functions. The LP relaxation of the problem is feasible (Proskurin's symmetric point), so the proof has to use
integrality.

**Certificate and checks:** [DennisKoshta/c37-degree-sensitivity-certificate](https://github.com/DennisKoshta/c37-degree-sensitivity-certificate/tree/472e2d95c85fe681826e70c90bc60a05ab5c0bc3) at commit `472e2d9`.

B = (1/D)[ Σ mⱼ log M(Rⱼ∘T) + ∫ max(0, Σ qᵢ log|Sᵢ∘T| − Σ mⱼ log|Rⱼ∘T|) ], where T(z) = z(1−z).

- **Denominators: 4, all new.** They are monic, irreducible and degree 104, pairwise coprime, with D = 999,999,999,960.
  - Their normalised log-Mahler measures are 0.252405–0.252442. For comparison, P₉ is 0.25272 and #301's degree-44 MD factors are 0.25308–0.25323.
  - None of the earlier denominators keeps positive weight.
- **Numerators: 24** (deg A / D = 0.9034):
  - Doche's P₁, P₂, P₃, P₄ and P₆;
  - MS192 and MS360 from #301;
  - one from the 27 Oct certificate;
  - **16 new** (degrees 10–42).
- **Weights:** multiplicities and exponents were re-optimised jointly by an LP on a 2¹⁹-point grid, then rounded exactly.

### How the denominators were found
This uses Pinho's reduced cost for a monic denominator and his residue-class restriction R = R₀ + X(X−1)P₄·U from #301. Two changes made the difference:

1. **Closest-vector step.** The weighted evaluation lattice is LLL-reduced on its own, and the closest points come from Schnorr–Euchner enumeration rather than Kannan embedding.
   - With embedding, the IRLS step almost never moved: the neighbours it offered cost about +0.3 in reduced cost.
   - With enumeration, candidates land within about 0.01, and the iteration keeps descending.
2. **Product starts.** Starting from products of library factors at degree 88 (44+44) and 104 (44+60) was far richer than degree 44.

The search alternated with the iterated dual-weighted LLL numerator search from the 27 Oct version, on a warm-started LP. The bound went:
- 0.2530918 → 0.25274 at degrees 44 and 60
- → 0.25265 at degree 88
- → 0.25245 at degree 104
- → 0.2524177 with a finer quadrature.

title: Add C_89c: Ramsey multiplicity constant of K_6, with a certified upper bound 0.7422548616·2^-14 (was 0.7445·2^-14)
body:
**Stacked on #277** (the 89b page and README rows): this branch carries #277's commit underneath. Once #277 is merged, only the second commit remains.

Adds **C_89c, the Ramsey multiplicity constant of $K_6$**, with a **new certified upper bound** $C_{89c} \le 0.7422548616 \cdot 2^{-14}$*. The previous best is $0.7445 \cdot 2^{-14}$ (Franek, Combinatorica 2002, exactly $51162598917 \cdot 2^{-50}$; Deza–Franek–Liu 2012), so the new bound is 0.30% lower. Markdown only: `constants/89c.md`, a README row and a "Recent progress" line.

**Construction.** Franek's bound comes from blow-ups of the Cayley graph on $\mathbb{Z}_2^{10}$ with $x \sim y$ iff $\lvert x \triangle y\rvert \in \{1,3,4,7,8,10\}$ (red inside the blocks). Keeping all its symmetries, the red density between blocks $x, y$ becomes a free function of the Hamming weight $\lvert x \triangle y\rvert$: 11 numbers in $[0,1]$. L-BFGS-B from Franek's 0/1 point gives $(1, 0.43996, 0, 1, 1, 0.01295, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0.76253)$, which is rounded to multiples of $2^{-20}$.

**Exact evaluation.** Fixing $x_0 = 0$, the density is a sum over the $\binom{41}{10} \approx 1.1 \times 10^9$ multisets of column types of $(x_1, \ldots, x_5)$; all 15 pair weights are column counts. Two separately written C programs compute the integer numerator modulo 61-bit primes, combined by CRT (6 primes plus a check prime). One is a DFS with incremental weights; the other iterates over count vectors and recomputes everything per leaf, sharing no code. Both give exactly

$180244428715156181493112659521741405180580225001966676111887908798425648907356856409/3978585891278293137243057985174566720803649206378781739523711815145275976100267004264448 = 0.742254861593625\ldots \cdot 2^{-14}$,

and both reproduce Franek's $51162598917/2^{50}$ from his parameters. Data and checkers are at [JeetuSK0808/tao-constants-certificates@98b6ee3](https://github.com/JeetuSK0808/tao-constants-certificates/tree/98b6ee34e8f51f82be85517e4b7f0e7e7af393b8/c89c-k6-ramsey-multiplicity). The bound is asterisked as self-hosted.

**Lower bound.** No dedicated lower bound for $c_6$ is in the literature; flag algebras of the size used for $c_4, c_5$ are out of reach. The page records the averaging bound $1/\binom{252}{6}$ from $R(6,6) \le \binom{10}{5}$ and cites Conlon's general bounds. Better published bounds on $R(6,6)$ improve it only marginally, and I kept the classical one rather than pick between conflicting recent figures.

title: Add C_89b: Ramsey multiplicity constant of K_5, with a certified upper bound 0.0016870052 (was 0.001708)
body:
Adds **C_89b, the Ramsey multiplicity constant of $K_5$** (the minimum density of monochromatic $K_5$ over 2-colourings of $K_n$), as a second member of the family of C_89 ($K_4$). It also records a **new certified upper bound**, $C_{89b} \le 0.0016870052$*. Markdown only: `constants/89b.md`, README rows (the existing 89 row is relabelled 89a), and a "Recent progress" line.

| side | bound | source |
|---|---|---|
| upper | $1/512$ | Erdős 1962 (random colouring; conjectured sharp) |
| upper | $0.001769$, $0.001720$ | Thomason 1989, 1997 (as summarised by PPSS) |
| upper | $2320651 \cdot 2^{-24} \cdot 3^{-4} < 0.001708$ | Parczyk–Pokutta–Spiegel–Szabó, FoCM 2024, Thm 1.2 (192-vertex Cayley graph) |
| upper | **$0.0016870052$*** | this PR, details below |
| lower | $0.001524$ | PPSS 2024, Thm 1.2 (flag algebras) |

The floating-point flag algebra value $0.001557$ of Kiem–Pokutta–Spiegel (arXiv:2312.08049), which they did not certify, is mentioned under "Additional comments" only.

**The new bound.** I start from the PPSS 192-vertex graph (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6602512, CC-BY-4.0) read as a step graphon: red between blocks joined by an edge, blue inside blocks. That reproduces their value. The density is computed **exactly over every pair of blocks**: the integer numerator $N(R) + N(2^{20} - R)$, with $N(R) = \sum_{i,j} R_{ij} \operatorname{tr}((\mathrm{diag}(R_i \circ R_j) R)^3)$, modulo 11 primes, combined by CRT, plus a check prime. The evaluator shares no code with the search, reproduces PPSS's $2320651/1358954496$ exactly, and agrees with brute force on small cases. The result is

$107218716425177032911811117405568916263805081691166740697/63555655070790142733837367909977622463036348875198349443072 = 0.0016870051344094\ldots$,

that is $2.07 \times 10^{-5}$ below PPSS. title: C68: improved lower bound 0.446 (flux and half-diameter lemmas)
body:
**C68 ≥ 0.446** (lower bound; previous 0.432* [Pin2026], before that 0.4263 [Wik2026]).

Certificate, proof and checkers: [vidigoat/optimization-records @ 1a76f9d, `tao/certificates/c68`](https://github.com/vidigoat/optimization-records/tree/1a76f9dd053d51cce531b57b2ad5a68e3205ca75/tao/certificates/c68).

**What changed.** The argument keeps Wikström's moment-duality criterion and Pinho's coefficient step, and sharpens the geometric input:

1. **Flux (period) lemma** (`PROOF.md`, Lemma 2). For ω: Ann → 𝔻 holomorphic with ω(z₁) = 0 and |z₁| = |z₂| = r,
   `−log|ω(z₂)| ≥ G(z₂, z₁) + σ·sech²(A/2)`, where σ = sin²(πφ(r)), φ(r) = 1 + log(r)/w, w = −log c, A = π²/w.
   Single-valuedness of ω makes the circle flux of −log|ω| an integer; the fluxes of the Green potentials G(·, b) are −φ_b or 1 − φ_b, the harmonic part's flux is bounded by its boundary means, and a uniform lower bound on the annulus Green function (Lemma 1) turns the integrality constraint into the extra term.
2. **Half-diameter enclosing lemma** (Lemma 5): with the pairwise bound from (1), each circle's image lies in a hyperbolic disk of radius D/2, replacing hyperbolic Jung's D/2 + log(2/√3).

Together G(t) = (1 + √(1 + Ψ/(2σ(t))))/2 with Ψ = (1+q)²/(8q), q = e^{−A}.

**Certificate.** c = 223/500, R = 99/100, 8 exact rational atoms plus Lebesgue measure on [R, 1]; every k is covered (direct checks for k ≤ 5806 / k ≤ 1349, analytic tail arguments beyond). Minimum relative margins 6.99·10⁻⁶. A second certificate gives 8921/20000 = 0.44605; exploratory LPs put the limit of this framework at about 0.44607.

**Verification.** Two independently written checkers (`check_c68.py`, Arb ball arithmetic at 320 bits; `check2_c68.py`, mpmath interval arithmetic) both pass, and both replay Pinho's 0.432 certificate with his margins. `mutation_tests.py` confirms both reject seven corrupted certificates.

**Status.** Unrefereed. The two lemmas are new; the key steps were re-read in a separate pass, but there has been no line-by-line human expert verification, so independent review is welcome. Prepared with Claude (Anthropic) agents under my direction, as stated on the page.

Each has a certificate and an exact or ball-arithmetic checker in [vidigoat/optimization-records](https://github.com/vidigoat/optimization-records/tree/9f82508a30d74b6b3c59c6f495269bd3bf4f61e5/tao/certificates). All are asterisked: self-archived and not yet independently replayed, except where a replay is noted below.

**Updated 4 Nov: C16 is now determined to 14 digits, and C1c is improved again.**

| Constant | New bound | Previous | Certificate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **16a** (upper) | **2.15622552815422** | 2.1562256466* | `c16_pinned/` |
| **16a** (lower) | **2.15622552815421** | 2.1562247706* on the page; 2.156225528* in #319 | `c16_pinned/`, `bgw_exact/` |
| **1c** (lower) | **0.4103540676** | 0.4103333* on the page; 0.4103538918* in #318 | `c1c_v2/`, `c1c/` |
| 1a (upper) | 1.5027433522 | 1.5027434868 | `c1a/` |
| 86a (upper) | 1.8077686 | 1.8084990* | `c86/` (independently replayed in the comments) |
| 89a (upper) | 0.0301388585 | 0.0301388794* | `c89/` |

### 16a: C16 = 2.1562255281542… (2.15622552815421 ≤ C16 ≤ 2.15622552815422)

**Upper bound.** This uses the Cauchy–Schwarz dual bound of the existing upper certificate (maximusrufus): 4π‖u‖∞²/‖∇u‖² ≤ G(μ)(1+μδ)/π, with G(μ) = Σ_{k≠0} 1/(|k|²(1+μ|k|²)). The bound is convex in δ, so on any δ-interval it suffices to check the two endpoints. Two changes make it tight:
1. **G(μ) is enclosed exactly.** Each row is summed with Σ_y 1/(y²+s²) = (π/s)coth(πs). The convex tail of rows is bracketed between a trapezoid and a midpoint sum with closed-form integrals, so there is no lattice truncation.
2. **A fine partition.** [1, 2¹⁸] is covered by 353 δ-intervals, each with its own optimised μ.

δ ≥ 2¹⁸ is handled with μ = 1/(δ ln δ) and lattice-point counting (#{0 < |k| ≤ R} ≤ π(R + 1/√2)²), which gives a bound of 2.0934.

The largest endpoint value, in Arb ball arithmetic, is 2.1562255281542197 ± 5·10⁻¹⁷. A brute-force lattice sum agrees with the enclosed G(μ) to the accuracy of the brute-force sum, and a rerun near the peak with twice as many terms at 256 bits gives the same result.

**Lower bound.** The untruncated conditional extremal, as in J. Julsgaard's #319, with μ = 0.122110476195 gives L ≥ 2.1562255281542128 (± 1.7·10⁻¹⁶). This agrees with #319's 2.1562255281542061 to 14 digits. The 7·10⁻¹⁵ difference comes only from a finer choice of μ.

**Why the two sides meet.** For each δ, the maximiser of |u(0)|² is the conditional-extremal family, and the Cauchy–Schwarz weights are exactly its dual. So the upper and lower bounds coincide, and the remaining work was numerical.

To reproduce: `python verify.py certificate.json` (about 15 s, python-flint) and `python lower.py 0.122110476195`.

### 1c: C1c ≥ 0.4103540676

A step function on K = 98304 cells. Exact value: 645458795582745374892957696 / 1572931393892132517694378321 = 0.41035406762757…, with the minimum at k = 93282. Two independently written exact scorers agree: 128-bit C over every lag, and one big-integer product.

It was refined from Julsgaard's certificate in #318 (0.4103538918*), which was itself refined from this PR's 26 Oct certificate. The refinement is L-BFGS on a soft minimum, in repeated cycles of re-softening (p = 10⁸) and re-sharpening (up to 10⁹). One run at fixed high sharpness stalls; the cycles keep gaining.

### Earlier entries (unchanged since 26–29 Oct)

- **1a:** refined from Atris's 65,536-step function to 262,144 steps. Exact value by one big-integer product.
- **86a:** Koshta's LP extended to the 2954 degree-8 polynomials with roots in [0, 5.3] and trace ≤ 16, on cells of width 1/400. Koshta's verifier reports `VALID 1.807768536863`. The margins are stated as corrected after the independent replay.
- **89a:** J. SK's 3840-block step graphon refined by L-BFGS. Exact density by CRT over 12 primes plus a check prime.

**Overlap with open PRs.** #318 and #319 add rows on the same pages, and whichever lands second will need a rebase. I'm happy to do it.

**Independent replay (86a).** A. Canli replayed the C86 certificate in this thread with separately written code: the exact bound is reproduced, and f ≥ 4.86·10⁻⁷ is certified on all 1,243 cells. The 86a row now records this. Per CONTRIBUTING, the asterisk can be removed at the maintainers' discretion; I have left it in place.

This PR offers that replay for the two C31 rows merged in #231, with no code shared with the claimant. Markdown only.

**What was replayed.** [J2026] runs Lueker's upper-bound method ([L2009], Theorem 3.3): an automaton $M_h$ over pairs of binary strings with history length $h$, a weight matrix $A_z$, and a positive vector $v$ with $A_z v \le \lambda v$, which gives $\gamma_2 \le 2\log(2z)/\log\lambda$. Lueker computed $h \le 8$; the two rows take $h = 9$ and $h = 10$.

| row | states (ours = [J2026]) | $z$ | our certified $\lambda$ | [J2026]'s $\lambda$ | our bound | printed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $h = 9$ | 51,425,006 | 0.3298 | $\le 0.364708361168896$ | 0.364708361184292 | $\gamma_2 \le 0.8251002730$ | $0.825101$ ✓ |
| $h = 10$ | 400,253,317 | 0.3376 | $\le 0.385532597279844$ | 0.385532705434511 | $\gamma_2 \le 0.8241195407$ | $0.824120$ ✓ |

Beside each certificate a certified **lower** bound on the spectral radius of $A_z$, $\rho \ge 0.364708361168863$ at $h = 9$ and $\rho \ge 0.385532597279807$ at $h = 10$ (the minimum ratio under downward rounding): no certificate for these automata can print a $\lambda$ below it, and both of [J2026]'s sit above it, by $1.5 \times 10^{-11}$ and $1.1 \times 10^{-7}$. Any positive vector certifies, so those are valid, less converged certificates, not errors; both printed bounds hold with room.

**How.** The automaton was written from [L2009] alone (the 2008 extended version, whose Figure 8 and Theorem 2 are the journal's Figure 7 and Theorem 3.3), twice: a Python reference in the standard library and a C builder, which share no code with each other or with [J2026] (its `src/` and `review/` were never fetched). The two give identical tables for $h \le 5$; at $h = 8$, $9$ and $10$ the C table was checked by re-deriving the transitions of 2,000, 2,000 and 1,000 random states in the reference, 0 mismatches; the complement symmetry of the state set was checked. The witness vectors are our own, from power iteration (294 and 338 passes); the certificate $\max_s (A_z v)_s / v_s$ is taken with the rounding mode set upward in every thread (self-tested) and the weights rounded up, once more in round-to-nearest with an explicit inflation; the bound $2\log(2z)/\log\lambda$ is evaluated outward in 60-digit decimal arithmetic. Every printed upper bound above is rounded up at its last digit, every lower bound down.

**Red controls**, which must come out wrong: the weights off by one power of $z$ and the truncation weight not summed both miss Lueker's $\lambda$ at $h = 8$; a claim below the certificate, $z = 1/2$, $\lambda = 1$, a vector with a zero entry, a vector of the wrong length and the all-ones vector are refused; a claimant $\lambda$ below the certified lower bound on $\rho$ is refuted. 9 of 9 fired.

## $C_{86}$ — the trace-constant certificate

**What was replayed.** The certificate `cert_n1200_A11.json` at rpinho/c86-trace-certificate commit `116a58f` (sha256 `722a287b74a9…`): a step measure $\mu$ on the cells of width $1/200$ (629 nonzero cells, support $[1/20, 1037/200]$) and eleven integer polynomials $Q$ with rational weights $b_Q$. The six finite conditions the row states — the hypotheses of Smith's sufficiency criterion [Smi24] and the arithmetic of the bound — were decided by two implementations sharing no code with each other (Python: `Fraction` and its own outward-rounded series logarithm; JavaScript: BigInt rationals and an interval library):

| | condition | how | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | $d_i \ge 0$, edges increasing, support inside $[1/20, 1037/200]$ | exact | holds |
| E2 | each $Q$ primitive, irreducible over $\mathbb{Z}$, totally real; the $Q$ distinct | exact (integer roots and monic quadratic factors within the Mignotte bound; Sturm counts) | holds for all eleven |
| E3 | $\sum_Q b_Q \deg Q < m$ | exact | $0.82978\,m$ |
| E4 | $\int \log\lvert Q\rvert\,d\mu > 0$ for each $Q$ | closed form in $g(u) = u\ln\lvert u\rvert - u$ at the edges, roots enclosed to $2^{-80}$, outward rounding | every lower end $> 0$ (each $\approx 10^{-4}$) |
| E5 | $U_\mu - \sum_Q b_Q \log\lvert Q\rvert \ge 0$ on the support | adaptive bisection; cell-edge terms by their exact monotone ranges, the smooth rest by a second-order Taylor form | proved on 3,658 boxes in both implementations, smallest certified lower bound $2.3 \times 10^{-8}$ |
| E6 | $\int x\,d\mu / m$ equals the certificate's bound and is $\le 1.8117251$ | exact | $144938007612277893/79999999999994000 = 1.81172509515360954\ldots$ |

**What was not re-derived.** The extension of E5 from the support to $\mathbb{C}$ (the minimum principle), the resultant argument that makes $\mu/m$ arithmetic, and Smith's theorem [Smi24] — published mathematics, cited by the row and read, not re-proved. The replay is of the certificate's finite conditions, which is what the asterisk is about.

title: 46a: the 4 − 2/15 bound is credited to Bourgain's GAFA 1991 paper, which proves 31/8
body:
The upper-bounds row `4 − 2/15 ≈ 3.86667` cites [Bo1991], Bourgain, *Besicovitch type maximal operators and applications to Fourier analysis*, GAFA 1 (1991) 147-187. That paper proves the exponent 31/8 (p. 185, "Take p₀ = 31/8", from Proposition 6.47 on p. 182) and does not state 58/15. The 58/15 bound is Proposition 2.15 of Bourgain's IHES preprint M/90/74, *On the restriction and multiplier problem in R³*, which the GAFA paper cites on p. 186 and lists on p. 187 as "to appear in Springer LNM".

A likely published form is Bourgain, *On the restriction and multiplier problems in R3*, in *Geometric Aspects of Functional Analysis*, Lecture Notes in Mathematics, Springer, 1991, pp. 179-191, doi:10.1007/BFb0089225. We have not read that chapter, so we cannot confirm that it contains the 58/15 result, or where; we identified it from its bibliographic record only. body:
## Summary

Two lower bounds for $C_{60}=\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}$, the Favard-length decay exponent of the four-corner Cantor set. The page currently records $1/6$ (Nazarov–Peres–Volberg).

1. **$\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}\ge 1/5$, by Caleb Marshall** ([arXiv:2509.02882](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02882), v2, 12 August 2026). Theorem 1.2, restated as Theorem 8.3: $\mathrm{Fav}(\mathcal N_{4^{-N}}(K^\infty))\le C_u N^{-1/5+u}$ for every $u>0$. This has not been recorded here yet.
2. **$\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}\ge 1/4$**, from a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization: https://github.com/CoolRmal/FavardLength at commit `65f19d4`, registered on the Palomar registry as [PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001&version=1). It proves $\mathrm{Fav}(K_n)\le C_a n^{-a}$ for every $a<1/4$.

## Credit, and the relation to Marshall's work

The $1/4$ proof is built on Marshall's. The formalized combinatorial dichotomy is an endpoint form of his marked-cylinder and packing construction (v2, section 7), which is what replaced NPV's $K^{2+o(1)}$ propagation by $K^{1+o(1)}$. What is added is analytic: a joint negative moment of the whole low-frequency product. Marshall's section 8.5 and his Future Directions identify a weighted low-frequency estimate as the missing input that would give $1/4-u$, and describe $1/5$ as a barrier for the methods there.

Two further points of attribution, both recorded on the page:

- The Fourier-analytic framework (normalized densities, Riesz products, exceptional directions) is Nazarov–Peres–Volberg's.
- **Version 1** of Marshall's preprint (2 September 2025) did assert $1/4$ for this set, in Remark 1.3 and section 3.5. **Version 2 withdraws that assertion**, saying the substitution that would yield $1/4-u$ "is not justified by our current methods". I have recorded the withdrawn claim in *Additional comments* so the history is visible rather than silently dropped.

## Verification

- Compared theorems: `favard_le_rpow_of_lt_quarter`, `one_quarter_le_decayExponent`, and `le_one_of_mem_admissibleExponents` / `decayExponent_le_one`. The last two reprove the known $\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}\le 1$ from an elementary $\mathrm{Fav}(K_n)\ge 1/(320n)$, which also shows the admissible set is bounded above, so $\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}$ is a genuine supremum. Nothing claims $1/4$ itself is admissible.
- `Challenge.lean` spells out $C_n$, $K_n$, $\pi_\theta$, projection length, $\mathrm{Fav}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}$ from Mathlib alone, and matches the definition on this page.
- No `sorry` outside the Challenge's statement holes, no `native_decide`; the axioms are `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. CI runs Lean Comparator against the challenge file and is green at the cited commit.
- The $1/4$ is registered on the Palomar registry ([PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001&version=1)), whose mechanical check reran Comparator in a sandbox and replayed the proof through Lean's kernel and the independent NanoDa kernel. Neither bound is refereed. If you prefer to mark either row with the unverified asterisk, please do; I have not added one.

- `constants/60a.md`: two new rows in *Known lower bounds*, a note in *Additional comments* about the withdrawn v1 claim, and `[Mar2026]` and `[Lin2026]` references.
- `README.md`: the $C_{60}$ lower-bound cell becomes $\frac{1}{4}$, plus two lines in *Recent progress*.

title: Numerical Exploration of $C_{10c}$ bounds via SDP Relaxations (CVXPY)
body:
Hello all,

I've been looking at the discrepancy bounds in the repository, specifically the unverified upper bound of $3.65^*$ for $C_{10c}$ (Spencer's constant). To explore the worst-case behavior numerically, I modeled a Bansal-style Semidefinite Relaxation (SDR) using CVXPY and the SCS solver for $n=512$.

**Empirical Findings ($n=512$):**
* **Structured Systems:** For a $512 \times 512$ subset of a Hadamard matrix, the SDR yields a tight lower bound of exactly $0.5\sqrt{n}$.
* **Unstructured Systems:** For a $512 \times 512$ random Bernoulli matrix ($p=0.5$), the SDR yields a highly relaxed bound of $\approx 0.027\sqrt{n}$.

**Discussion:**
These numerical results cleanly illustrate the theoretical expectation: random instances are "soft" in the SDR, while structured orthogonality (Hadamard) raises the bound. However, both fall vastly short of the $3.67$ universal constant. This suggests that any computational effort to strictly verify or tighten the $3.65^*$ bound using relaxations will require generating highly correlated, adversarial non-orthogonal incidence matrices.

If the maintainers are interested, I would be happy to submit a PR adding this CVXPY formulation to a `/scripts` directory so others can easily benchmark specific adversarial set systems against these relaxations.
